content.value_statement: Angular applications often lose speed through costly change detection, oversized bundles, and avoidable hydration work. This skill gives prioritized review guidance for faster components, routes, and SSR.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Angular components for OnPush, Signals, selector usage, and template complexity.
Identifies async waterfalls and suggests parallel or flattened data fetching patterns.
Guides lazy loading, deferred views, direct imports, and third-party library splitting.
Checks SSR and hydration patterns, including TransferState and non-critical content deferral.
Flags rendering and memory issues such as missing track expressions, manual subscriptions, and unvirtualized lists.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not an automated Angular compiler or profiler.
It does not run benchmarks, inspect production telemetry, or measure real browser performance.
Recommendations may need adjustment for older Angular versions or strict project constraints.
It cannot verify dependency sizes without project build outputs or bundle reports.

use_cases.title: Review a New Component
use_cases.description: Check a component for modern Angular performance patterns before it reaches code review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Performance Refactor
use_cases.description: Rank improvements across change detection, routes, rendering, SSR, and subscriptions.

use_cases.title: Audit SSR and Hydration
use_cases.description: Find client-side waterfalls, missing server data transfer, and non-critical hydration work.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular component for change detection, template work, and subscription cleanup using the angular-best-practices skill.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Feature Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized refactor plan for this Angular feature to reduce bundle size, improve rendering, and protect SSR hydration.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these Angular implementation options for Signals, selectors, deferred loading, and route data fetching. Recommend the lowest-risk approach.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Application Slice
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Angular application slice for performance risks. Group findings by impact, migration cost, and user-visible benefit.

output_examples.input: A dashboard component uses default change detection, manual subscriptions, and expensive template calculations.
output: Highest impact: adopt OnPush and Signals for local state to reduce unnecessary checks.
Next: move expensive derived values into cached component state or a pure pipe.
Cleanup: replace manual subscription handling with framework-managed teardown.

output_examples.input: An admin route eagerly loads charts, tables, and feature components in the main bundle.
output: Split the admin route from the initial bundle and load it only when users navigate there.
Defer heavy visual sections until they enter the viewport or require user interaction.
Import large third-party libraries only inside the workflow that needs them.

output_examples.input: An SSR page fetches critical profile data only after browser JavaScript starts.
output: Move critical data loading into a server-ready route resolver or equivalent preloading step.
Use server-to-browser state transfer to avoid duplicate fetches after hydration.
Defer non-critical widgets so first content stays focused on user-visible data.

best_practices: Start reviews with the highest impact areas: change detection, async fetching, and bundle loading.
Ask for Angular version, route structure, and SSR usage before applying advanced recommendations.
Pair each recommendation with expected performance impact and migration cost.
anti_patterns: Treating every rule as mandatory without checking product constraints.
Optimizing small templates before fixing data waterfalls or large eager bundles.
Adding manual subscriptions when Signals or framework cleanup utilities fit the use case.

faq.question: Which Angular versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on modern Angular patterns such as Signals, OnPush, deferred views, SSR, and hydration. Older projects may need adapted guidance.

faq.question: Can it rewrite my Angular code?
faq.answer: It can suggest refactors and review pasted code. File edits depend on the AI tool and permissions you use with the skill.

faq.question: Does this skill require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-based and uses reference links only.

faq.question: How is it different from generic Angular help?
faq.answer: It prioritizes performance decisions by impact, from change detection and data fetching to bundles, SSR, templates, and cleanup.

faq.question: Can it help with SSR performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers route data loading, hydration behavior, non-critical content deferral, and server-to-browser state transfer.

faq.question: Is it a substitute for profiling?
faq.answer: No. Use browser profiling, bundle reports, and production metrics to validate the recommendations.
